analysis:
Examined base_text Messages.swift lines 653-1717: ProviderMessage encode/decode, the CodingKeys enum and the CoordinatorMessage structs. The file_changes map shows that the head adds an optional `busy: ProviderBusy?` field to Register (head 248-251, 281-286) and to Heartbeat (head 344-366). It also adds coding keys around head 948-951 and encode lines around head 1070/1097. Decode changes are at head 1345-1346 and 1371-1372; base lines 1328 and 1353 were modified to append a busy decode. The field is omitted when nil.

Security relevance: busy is provider-authored advisory routing state. It reports draining status, reason, since_ms and add-on, and it is intended to exclude a connection from routing before its first heartbeat. A malicious provider (ADV-001) can only use it to make itself less routable. That is self-denial of service, not escalation.

It does not touch attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052/T-053), encryption (T-008), cache receipts (T-041) or billing fields.

Possible privacy concern: busy_addon and busy_since_ms could expose local add-on identity and activity timing to the coordinator. This is provider-operator telemetry, not consumer data. ProviderBusy's definition and its encoding are not visible in the supplied units.

Integration questions:
- Confirm that ProviderBusy's strings are bounded or enumerated.
- Confirm the coordinator treats busy only as a routing exclusion and never as a trust signal.
- Confirm that decoding an unknown busy_reason fails tolerantly rather than rejecting register/heartbeat messages.

No regression identified in the visible units.
